design_intent: 4-bit shift register that shifts left by one bit on each rising clock edge when enable is high. Reset clears the register to zero.
explanation: The module uses blocking assignments inside clocked sequential logic. That can cause incorrect update ordering because later assignments may use values that were already changed earlier in the same clock event. Non-blocking assignments make all register updates happen together at the clock edge, which is the intended behaviour for a shift register.
verification_suggestion: Apply a known serial bit pattern over several clock cycles and verify that each bit moves one position per clock. Also, verify that reset clears q to 0000.

design_intent: 8-bit counter that increments by one on each rising clock edge when enable is high. Active-high reset should immediately clear the counter to zero.
explanation: The reset logic is wrong because reset is checked after enable and is not included in the sensitivity of the sequential block. That means reset will not act as intended when asserted. The fix gives reset the highest priority and adds it to the event control so the counter clears immediately on reset.
verification_suggestion: Assert reset while enable is both high and low and confirm count becomes zero immediately. Then deassert reset and verify counting resumes correctly.

design_intent: Modulo-10 counter that counts from 0 to 9 and then wraps back to 0 on the next clock edge when enable is high. Reset clears the counter to zero.
explanation: The wrap condition is wrong. A modulo-10 counter should wrap after reaching 9, not 10. In the buggy version the counter reaches 10, which violates the intended range of 0 through 9. The fix changes the terminal comparison to 9.
verification_suggestion: Run the counter through at least 12 enabled clock cycles and confirm the sequence goes 0 through 9, then wraps to 0. Also check reset behavior.

design_intent: 4-to-1 combinational multiplexer that routes one of four 8-bit inputs to the output based on a 2-bit select signal.
explanation: The combinational logic does not assign y for every possible select value. That can lead to unintended latch behavior or undefined output behavior. The fix adds the missing select case and a default assignment so y is always driven.
verification_suggestion: Test all four select values and confirm y matches the correct input each time. Also confirm output is always driven for any possible sel value.

design_intent: Two-stage pipeline register. When enable is high, din should appear at dout after two rising clock edges. Reset clears all registers to zero.
explanation: The sequential block uses blocking assignments, so stage1 is updated before dout in the same clock event. That collapses the intended two-stage pipeline behavior because dout can see the new value too early. Non-blocking assignments preserve the intended cycle-by-cycle register transfer.
verification_suggestion: Drive din with a changing bit pattern while enable stays high and verify that dout reflects each input value exactly two clock cycles later. Also confirm reset clears both pipeline stages.

design_intent: 8-bit loadable register with active-low asynchronous reset. When rst_n is low, q should immediately clear to zero. When rst_n is high and load is asserted, q should capture d on the rising clock edge.
explanation: The reset polarity is backwards. This module is supposed to have an active-low reset, so the register must clear when rst_n is 0, not when it is 1. In the buggy version, the register gets cleared when reset is deasserted and fails to reset when reset is actually asserted.
verification_suggestion: Pull rst_n low and confirm q clears immediately. Then release rst_n, assert load, and verify q captures d only on the next rising clock edge.

design_intent: Simple gate controller FSM with three states: CLOSED, OPENING, and OPEN. When sensor is asserted in CLOSED, the gate should move to OPENING. When open_done is asserted in OPENING, the gate should move to OPEN. When timeout is asserted in OPEN, the gate should return to CLOSED.
explanation: The OPENING state transitions to CLOSED when open_done is asserted, which skips the OPEN state entirely. That breaks the intended behavior because the controller never enters the state where the gate is considered fully open. The fix changes that transition so OPENING moves to OPEN when the opening operation finishes.
verification_suggestion: After reset, assert sensor to enter OPENING, then assert open_done and confirm the FSM moves to OPEN. Finally assert timeout and confirm it returns to CLOSED.

design_intent: Pulse generator that asserts tick for one clock cycle every 5 enabled clock cycles. Reset clears the internal counter and tick output to zero.
explanation: The counter is too narrow. A 2-bit register can only represent values 0 through 3, so it can never reach 4. That means the terminal-count condition is unreachable and tick will never assert as intended. The fix widens the counter so the value 4 can actually be represented.
verification_suggestion: Keep enable high and count clock cycles between tick pulses. Tick should go high once every 5 enabled cycles. Also verify reset clears the sequence and restarts the timing.

design_intent: 4-input priority encoder. If multiple request bits are high, the highest-index request has priority. valid should be high when any request is asserted and low otherwise.
explanation: The combinational block does not assign code or valid when no request bits are high. That can infer latches or leave stale values hanging around from a previous evaluation. The fix gives both outputs default values before the priority logic so they are always driven.
verification_suggestion: Check all single-request cases and confirm the highest asserted bit is encoded correctly. Also test req = 4'b0000 and verify valid is low and code returns to its default value.

design_intent: 4-bit byte counter with active-low asynchronous reset. When rst_n is low, count should clear immediately to zero. When rst_n is high, count increments on each rising clock edge if count_en is high.
explanation: The event control uses posedge rst_n even though the reset is active low. That means the always_ff block reacts when reset is released instead of when it is asserted. The fix changes the reset edge to negedge rst_n so the counter clears immediately when reset goes low.
verification_suggestion: Let the counter increment for a few cycles, then drive rst_n low between clocks and verify count clears immediately. Release rst_n and confirm counting resumes only on rising clock edges when count_en is high.

design_intent: Simple request/acknowledge handshake controller with three states: IDLE, WAIT_ACK, and DONE. A start pulse moves the FSM from IDLE to WAIT_ACK. An ack pulse in WAIT_ACK should move it to DONE. The FSM returns to IDLE on the next cycle from DONE.
explanation: The WAIT_ACK state transitions back to itself when ack is asserted, so the FSM never reaches DONE. That breaks the intended handshake completion behavior because done_pulse is never generated. The fix changes the acknowledged transition so the controller moves from WAIT_ACK to DONE.
verification_suggestion: Apply start and confirm the FSM enters WAIT_ACK with busy high. Then assert ack and verify the FSM moves to DONE for one cycle before returning to IDLE.

design_intent: Enable pulse generator. When en is high, tick should assert for one clock cycle every 4 enabled clock cycles. Reset clears the counter and tick output.
explanation: The terminal count is off by one. To generate a pulse every 4 enabled cycles, the counter must count 0, 1, 2, 3 before resetting. In the buggy version it resets when count reaches 2, so tick asserts every 3 enabled cycles instead of every 4.
verification_suggestion: Keep en high and count the number of enabled clock cycles between tick pulses. Confirm tick appears once every 4 enabled cycles and that reset restarts the sequence from the beginning.

design_intent: Three-state packet receiver FSM. IDLE waits for start. RECEIVE stays active while byte_valid is high. DONE should be entered for one cycle when last_byte is high, then the FSM returns to IDLE.
explanation: The RECEIVE state goes directly back to IDLE when last_byte is asserted, so the FSM skips the DONE state and never produces the one-cycle done pulse. The fix changes the last_byte transition so RECEIVE moves to DONE first.
verification_suggestion: Start a packet, assert last_byte while in RECEIVE, and verify the FSM enters DONE for exactly one cycle before returning to IDLE.

design_intent: 16-bit register with synchronous active-high reset and load enable. On each rising clock edge, reset has priority over load. If reset is high, q clears to zero. Else if load is high, q captures d.
explanation: Reset is checked after load, so when reset and load are both high the register captures d instead of clearing. The fix gives reset priority by checking rst before load.
verification_suggestion: Assert rst and load at the same rising clock edge and verify q clears to zero. Then deassert rst and confirm load captures d normally.

design_intent: Two-register delay chain. When en is high, a should capture din and b should capture the previous value of a on the same rising clock edge. Reset clears both registers.
explanation: The clocked block uses blocking assignments, so b can receive the newly assigned value of a instead of the previous-cycle value. Non-blocking assignments preserve the intended register-to-register delay behavior.
verification_suggestion: Drive two different din values on consecutive enabled clock cycles and verify b lags din by two pipeline stages. Also verify reset clears both registers.

design_intent: Timer that asserts expired for one clock cycle after 8 enabled cycles. Reset clears count and expired. The counter should count 0 through 7 and assert expired when count reaches 7.
explanation: A 3-bit counter can represent values 0 through 7, so the comparison to 8 can never be true. The expired pulse is unreachable. The fix compares count against 7, the last representable value in the intended 8-cycle sequence.
verification_suggestion: Keep en high and verify expired pulses once after the counter reaches 7. Also confirm reset clears the counter and restarts the timing sequence.

design_intent: 2-to-4 combinational decoder with enable. When en is high, exactly one bit of y should be high based on sel. When en is low, y should be 0000.
explanation: The output y is not assigned when en is low, so combinational logic may retain its previous value. The fix assigns y a default value of 0000 before the enabled decode logic.
verification_suggestion: Test all sel values with en high and verify one-hot outputs. Then set en low after different previous outputs and confirm y always becomes 0000.

design_intent: Three-state controller with states IDLE, RUN, and ERROR. Active-high reset should return the controller to IDLE. If start is asserted in IDLE, the FSM enters RUN. If fault is asserted in RUN, the FSM enters ERROR.
explanation: The reset branch sends the FSM to ERROR instead of IDLE, which violates the intended reset behavior. The fix resets the state register to IDLE so the controller starts in the safe idle state.
verification_suggestion: Assert reset and verify running is low and error is low. Then release reset, apply start, and confirm the FSM enters RUN normally.

design_intent: Two 8-bit registers that swap values on a rising clock edge when swap is high. Reset clears both registers. The swap must happen simultaneously using the previous values of both registers.
explanation: The swap uses blocking assignments in clocked logic, so b can receive the newly assigned value of a instead of the old value. Non-blocking assignments make both registers update together using their previous values.
verification_suggestion: Initialize a and b to different values, assert swap for one clock, and verify the values exchange rather than both becoming the same.

design_intent: Running sum register. On each rising clock edge when en is high, prev_sum should hold the old sum value and sum should add sample to its previous value. Reset clears both registers.
explanation: Blocking assignments cause prev_sum to capture the newly updated sum instead of the previous-cycle sum. The fix uses non-blocking assignments so prev_sum receives the old sum value while sum updates for the next cycle.
verification_suggestion: Apply a sequence of samples and verify prev_sum always equals the sum value from the previous enabled clock cycle. Also verify reset clears both outputs.

design_intent: 2-bit saturating counter. When inc is high, count should increment until it reaches 3 and then stay at 3. Reset clears count to zero.
explanation: A 2-bit counter can only represent values 0 through 3, so comparing count to 4 can never work as intended. The buggy counter rolls over instead of saturating. The fix detects count 3 and holds that value when inc remains high.
verification_suggestion: Assert inc for more than four clock cycles and verify count reaches 3 and stays there. Also verify reset returns count to 0.

design_intent: Sequence detector FSM for detecting input pattern 101. The FSM should assert detected for one cycle when the final 1 arrives. Overlapping sequences are allowed.
explanation: After detecting 101, the FSM returns to S0, which loses the final 1 even though overlapping sequences are allowed. The fix transitions to S1 after detection because the last input bit can also serve as the first bit of the next pattern.
verification_suggestion: Apply an overlapping stream such as 10101 and verify detected pulses twice. Also test nonmatching sequences to confirm detected stays low.

design_intent: Unsigned 8-bit comparator. Exactly one of lt, eq, or gt should be high for every input combination: lt when a < b, eq when a == b, and gt when a > b.
explanation: The combinational block only assigns the flag that is true and leaves the others unassigned, so old flag values can be retained. The fix assigns defaults to all flags before setting the selected output.
verification_suggestion: Test cases where a < b, a == b, and a > b in sequence, and verify exactly one flag is high each time with no stale flags left over.

design_intent: Small combinational control decoder. For mode 00 output cmd should be 001, for mode 01 cmd should be 010, for mode 10 cmd should be 100, and for mode 11 cmd should be 000.
explanation: The case statement does not assign cmd for mode 11, so the combinational output can retain a previous value. The fix adds the missing mode 11 branch and a default assignment.
verification_suggestion: Cycle through all four mode values and verify cmd matches the design intent every time, especially mode 11 after previously selecting a nonzero command.

design_intent: Two-state toggle FSM. Reset returns the FSM to A. When tick is high on a rising clock edge, the FSM toggles between A and B. When tick is low, it holds its current state.
explanation: The FSM gets stuck in state B because the B state transitions back to itself when tick is high. Since tick is the advance signal, B should transition to A on tick, while holding state when tick is low.
verification_suggestion: After reset, apply multiple tick pulses and verify the FSM alternates A, B, A, B. Also verify that when tick is low, the current state does not change.

design_intent: Three-state step FSM. Reset returns to S0. Each tick pulse advances the FSM from S0 to S1, S1 to S2, and S2 back to S0. When tick is low, the FSM holds its current state.
explanation: The S2 state incorrectly transitions back to itself when tick is high, so the FSM cannot wrap back to S0. The fix keeps tick as the advance condition and changes the S2 tick transition to S0.
verification_suggestion: Apply three tick pulses after reset and verify the sequence S0, S1, S2, S0. Also verify the FSM holds its state during cycles where tick is low.

design_intent: Two-state LED blink FSM. Reset returns to OFF. On each tick pulse, the FSM toggles OFF to ON or ON to OFF. If tick is low, the LED state should hold.
explanation: The ON state uses !tick as the transition condition, so the FSM turns off when tick is low instead of holding. Tick is supposed to be the advance pulse, so both transitions should happen when tick is high.
verification_suggestion: Hold tick low and verify the LED state does not change. Then apply tick pulses and verify the LED toggles once per pulse.

design_intent: Four-phase controller. Reset starts in PH0. Each tick pulse advances one phase: PH0 to PH1, PH1 to PH2, PH2 to PH3, and PH3 back to PH0. The phase must hold when tick is low.
explanation: The PH1 transition skips PH2 and jumps directly to PH3. The FSM should advance exactly one phase per tick. The fix changes the PH1 tick transition to PH2.
verification_suggestion: Apply tick pulses after reset and verify the phase sequence PH0, PH1, PH2, PH3, PH0. Also verify no phase changes occur while tick is low.

design_intent: Two-light traffic FSM. Reset starts in GREEN. On each tick pulse, the FSM toggles between GREEN and RED. When tick is low, the current light remains active.
explanation: The RED state transitions to GREEN when tick is low, but tick is supposed to be the advance pulse. The FSM should hold RED while tick is low and transition back to GREEN only when tick is high.
verification_suggestion: After reset, pulse tick and verify GREEN changes to RED. Keep tick low and verify the FSM stays RED. Pulse tick again and verify it returns to GREEN.

design_intent: Three-position selector FSM. Reset starts at POS0. Each tick pulse advances POS0 to POS1, POS1 to POS2, and POS2 back to POS0. Tick low means hold the current position.
explanation: The POS2 state wraps to POS0 when tick is low, which violates the hold behavior. The wrap should happen on tick, just like the other state advances. The fix changes the POS2 transition condition from !tick to tick.
verification_suggestion: Apply tick pulses and verify POS0, POS1, POS2, POS0. Hold tick low in each state and verify the selector does not move.

design_intent: Two-state toggle FSM. Reset returns to S0. When tick is high, the FSM toggles between S0 and S1. When tick is low, it holds its current state.
explanation: The FSM gets stuck in S1 because the S1 state transitions back to itself when tick is high. Since tick is the toggle signal, S1 should transition back to S0 on tick. When tick is low, the default next_state assignment already holds the current state.
verification_suggestion: After reset, apply repeated tick pulses and verify the FSM alternates S0, S1, S0, S1. Also hold tick low in each state and verify the state does not change.

design_intent: Two-state FSM. Reset starts in LEFT. A tick pulse is the only event that advances the FSM. On tick high, LEFT goes to RIGHT and RIGHT goes to LEFT. When tick is low, the FSM must hold its current state.
explanation: The FSM gets stuck in RIGHT because RIGHT transitions back to itself when tick is high. The correct fix is to make RIGHT transition to LEFT on tick. Do not change this to !tick, because tick is the advance pulse and tick low means hold state.
verification_suggestion: Apply repeated tick pulses and verify LEFT, RIGHT, LEFT, RIGHT. Hold tick low in each state and verify the FSM does not change state.

design_intent: Two-state S0/S1 FSM. Reset starts in S0. Every tick pulse toggles the state. If tick is low, the FSM holds the current state.
explanation: The S1 state loops back to itself when tick is high, so the FSM gets stuck in S1. Since tick is the toggle signal, the S1 transition should go to S0 when tick is high. Using !tick would be wrong because tick low is supposed to hold the state.
verification_suggestion: Pulse tick several times and verify the state sequence S0, S1, S0, S1. Also keep tick low and verify the FSM remains in its current state.
